# and GITHUB_TOKEN MAY trigger workflow_dispatch, 2022-09-08
  # changelog). The dispatch arm runs the full gate on the tag's exact
  # tree: release-pending never blocks dispatch arms (gh-1551) and
  # release-dedupe is false for non-release events (gh-1625 AC3).
  watchdog:
    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963;
    # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in
    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
    # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual]
    # Same-repo PRs: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref. Tag pushes: the
    # release gate (gh-2290).
    if: always() && ((github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository) || (github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')))
    permissions:
      actions: write # gh workflow run — the tag-arm retrigger (gh-2290)
      contents: write
    steps:
      # gh-2290: the trip decision runs a REPO script — a hosted runner's
      # empty workspace has no scripts/ (the exit-127 class reddened the
      # dedupe pre-check on every arm, runs 38696670029/38696668627). The
      # checkout must be UNCONDITIONAL — the trip step runs on every arm
      # this job reaches, and a skipped checkout would empty the trip
      # output. Shallow: the script never reads history.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1

      # One jobs call in a SINGLE valid document (steps arrays are
      # embedded per job — no per-job follow-ups; `gh api --paginate`
      # concatenates page bodies and jq then reads only the first page —
      # verified against a 69-job run), then the extracted,
      # fixture-self-tested trip decision (scripts/watchdog_trip_check.sh;
      # static-gate selftest: scripts/watchdog_trip_selftest.sh). It trips
      # ONLY on the timeout-kill signature — job conclusion `failure` OR
      # `cancelled` (the v1.0.745 kill landed as plain `cancelled`) with
      # at least one `cancelled` step and NO `failed` step — and never on
      # a real test failure (a step failed, regardless of which step is
      # last), a skip, or a cancelled never-started job.
      - name: Detect a timeout-type failure
        id: trip
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          gh run view "$RUN_ID" --repo "$REPO" --json jobs > watchdog-jobs.json
          bash scripts/watchdog_trip_check.sh watchdog-jobs.json
          bash scripts/watchdog_trip_check.sh watchdog-jobs.json

      # ── PR arm: empty-commit push (unchanged remedy) ──────────────────
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: steps.trip.outputs.trip == 'true' && github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger workflows — the retrigger must
          # re-fire CI, so it rides RELEASE_PAT (same as release/gardener).
          token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}

      - name: Retrigger with an empty commit (fresh runner allocation)
        if: steps.trip.outputs.trip == 'true' && github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          HAS_PAT: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT != '' }}
        run: |
          if [ "$HAS_PAT" != "true" ]; then
            echo "::notice::RELEASE_PAT not configured — cannot retrigger"
            exit 0
          fi
          msg="ci: watchdog retrigger (degraded runner pool)"
          if [ "$(git log -1 --format=%s)" = "$msg" ]; then
            echo "head commit is already a watchdog retrigger — not looping"
            exit 0
          fi
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git commit --allow-empty -m "$msg"
          git push origin HEAD:"${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}"

      # ── Tag arm (gh-2290): dispatch a fresh gate run on the tag ref ────
      # ONE retrigger max per tag (issue #194 loop-guard rule): a prior
      # workflow_dispatch run for this tag ref means the retrigger already
      # fired for this kill — never chain dispatches on a stuck pool.
      - name: Retrigger the tag gate (dispatch, fresh runner allocation)
        if: steps.trip.outputs.trip == 'true' && github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          prior=$(gh run list --workflow ci.yml --branch "$REF" \
            --event workflow_dispatch \
            --json databaseId --jq 'length' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
          if [ "${prior:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "::notice::a workflow_dispatch gate run already exists for $REF — not re-firing (one retrigger max per tag, gh-2290)"
            exit 0
          fi
          gh workflow run ci.yml --ref "$REF"
          echo "::notice::dispatched a fresh ci.yml gate run on $REF (watchdog degraded-runner retrigger, gh-2290)"

    name: Provider smoke (LLM, tag-only)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 20

    # #1368: the gate check reads the dart_ok OUTPUT, not the aggregate
    # result — a platform-only red (Windows build, PTY leg) used to skip this
    # smoke transitively and with it the publish job (the v1.0.519-521
    # starvation). dart_ok=false (a red package leg) still skips it: the
    # publish it gates cannot run anyway.
    if: >-

    env:
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copyright (c) 2026, the Flutter Agent Harness authors.
# Use of this source code is governed by a MIT license that can be found
# in the LICENSE file.
#
# watchdog_trip_check.sh — the gh-2290 timeout-kill trip decision for the
# `watchdog` job of .github/workflows/ci.yml (issue #194 point 4).
#
# The watchdog's remedy for a degraded-runner allocation is ONE retrigger
# with a fresh allocation (never `gh run rerun`). Tripping requires
# recognizing a job-level timeout KILL — and only that kill. The v1.0.745
# tag run 4424840840 hung a PTY shard (the pty2 blocking-waitpid wedge,
# `Attempt:N waiting for isolate _waitForExitCode to check in`), burned
# its 40-minute budget and was killed by `timeout-minutes`: GitHub landed
# that kill as job conclusion `cancelled` (NOT `failure` — jobs
# 134588877581/134566192421) with the mid-flight step `cancelled` and the
# trailing `if: always()` evidence steps `skipped`.
#
# The timeout-kill signature, as one predicate over the jobs JSON:
#
#   job conclusion == "failure" OR "cancelled"      (both kill shapes land)
#   AND at least one step concluded "cancelled"      (a step was cut
#     mid-flight — the kill itself)
#   AND NO step concluded "failure"                  (a real test failure
#     ENDS with a failed step — in these shards the `if: always()`
#     evidence steps often trail it with `success` — so a genuine red
#     never trips; a fresh runner allocation cannot fix a defect)
#
# A cancelled job with NO steps (never started — a run-level cancel
# reaching a queued job) is NOT a kill. Success/skipped never trip.
#
# Network-free by contract: the caller fetches the run's jobs document in
# ONE call (the jobs API embeds each job's steps array — `gh run view
# --json jobs`; `gh api .../runs/<id>/jobs` is fine unpaged, but
# `--paginate` concatenates page bodies and jq then reads only the first
# page — verified against a 69-job run) and hands the FILE here.
# Fixture-self-tested by scripts/watchdog_trip_selftest.sh (#1100
# pattern), wired into the static gate; the workflow wiring is pinned by
# test/ci_watchdog_tag_retrigger_guard_test.dart.
#
# Usage: watchdog_trip_check.sh [jobs-json-file] [output-file]
#   jobs-json-file  the jobs document; `-` or an empty arg reads stdin
#   output-file     default $GITHUB_OUTPUT when set (the trip=<bool> line
#                   lands there AND on stdout); without one, stdout only.
#                   Diagnostics never start with `trip=`, so the line is
#                   unambiguous in both sinks.
set -u

json_file="${1:--}"
out_file="${2:-${GITHUB_OUTPUT:-}}"

if [ "$json_file" = "-" ] || [ -z "$json_file" ]; then
  jobs_json="$(cat)"
else
  jobs_json="$(cat "$json_file")"
fi

# The timeout-kill signature, as one jq projection:
#   failed-or-cancelled jobs with >=1 cancelled step and NO failed step.
projection='
  [.jobs[]?
   | select(.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")
   | select(any(.steps[]?; .conclusion == "cancelled"))
   | select(all(.steps[]?; .conclusion != "failure"))]
  | length'

matches="$(printf '%s' "$jobs_json" | jq -r "$projection")"

if [ -z "$matches" ] || ! [ "$matches" -eq "$matches" ] 2>/dev/null; then
  # A malformed projection must NEVER flip the trip (fail-safe: the
  # watchdog is an optimization — a broken pre-check degrades to no
  # retrigger, never to a spurious dispatch loop).
  echo "::warning::watchdog_trip_check: unparseable jobs JSON or jq failure — not tripping"
  matches=0
fi

trip=false
if [ "$matches" -gt 0 ]; then
  trip=true
fi

if [ "$trip" = "true" ]; then
  echo "::notice::watchdog_trip_check: $matches job(s) match the timeout-kill signature (gh-2290):"
  printf '%s' "$jobs_json" | jq -r "$projection | .[]" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || true
  printf '%s' "$jobs_json" | jq -r '
    [.jobs[]?
     | select(.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")
     | select(any(.steps[]?; .conclusion == "cancelled"))
     | select(all(.steps[]?; .conclusion != "failure"))]
    | (.[] | "  " + .name + ": " + .conclusion
       + " (cancelled step: "
       + ([.steps[]? | select(.conclusion == "cancelled") | .name] | join(", "))
       + ")")'
else
  echo "watchdog_trip_check: no timeout-kill signature — nothing to retrigger"
fi

if [ -n "$out_file" ]; then
  {
    printf 'trip=%s\n' "$trip"
  } >> "$out_file"
fi
echo "trip=$trip"

# ci.yml).

# blocking-waitpid wedge (`Attempt:N waiting for isolate _waitForExitCode

#   AC1  the gh-2290 kill mode: job conclusion `cancelled`, the
#     mid-flight step `cancelled`, trailing `if: always()` evidence
#     steps `skipped` — the EXACT shape of hung shard jobs
#     134588877581/134566192421 → trip,
#   AC2  the classic kill mode: job `failure`, a cut `cancelled` step,
#     no failed step → trip,
#   FC1  a REAL test failure never trips — in either landing shape: the
#     failed step LAST, or the failed step TRAILED by the `if: always()`
#     evidence steps (`success`) that every red pty shard actually
#     leaves behind (last-step-success — the old last-step detector was
#     blind to this too),
#   FC2  success / skipped / a cancelled never-started job (no steps) /
#     an empty jobs array never trip,
#   FC3  a malformed body fails SAFE to trip=false with a warning (a
#     broken pre-check must degrade to no retrigger, never to a
#     spurious dispatch loop),
#   RG   the output contract: exactly ONE `trip=<bool>` line, no
#     diagnostic masquerading as `trip=`, GITHUB_OUTPUT lands exactly
#     one line, multiple matches still produce a single line, and the
#     stdin arm (`-`) works.
# Same discipline as release_dedupe_selftest.sh (gh-1625, #1100 pattern).
set -u
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
CHECK="$HERE/watchdog_trip_check.sh"
TMP="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

fails=0
check() { # check <desc> <condition-exit-code: 0 = pass>
  if [ "$2" = "0" ]; then
    echo "  ok: $1"
  else
    echo "  FAIL: $1"
    fails=$((fails + 1))
  fi
}

fixture() { # fixture <name> <json> — write a fixture, run the check
  _fx_name="$1"; shift
  printf '%s' "$1" > "$TMP/$_fx_name.json"
  bash "$CHECK" "$TMP/$_fx_name.json" 2>&1
}

trip_line() { # trip_line <output> — the trip= line, empty when absent
  printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -E '^trip=(true|false)$' | head -1
}

trip_count() { # trip_count <output> — number of trip= lines
  printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -cE '^trip=(true|false)$'
}

json_for() { # json_for <conclusion> <shape: kill|failure|success>
  # kill:    the REAL gh-2290 shape — the mid-flight dart test step
  #          cancelled, the trailing if:always() evidence steps skipped.
  # failure: a real test failure — the dart test step FAILED, the
  #          evidence steps still trail with success (the last step is
  #          NOT the failed one in these shards).
  # success: a clean job.
  case "$2" in
    kill)    steps='[{"name": "dart test", "conclusion": "cancelled"}, {"name": "junit durations", "conclusion": "skipped"}, {"name": "upload artifact", "conclusion": "skipped"}, {"name": "Post cache", "conclusion": "skipped"}]' ;;
    failure) steps='[{"name": "dart test", "conclusion": "failure"}, {"name": "junit durations", "conclusion": "success"}]' ;;
    *)       steps='[{"name": "run", "conclusion": "success"}]' ;;
  esac
  cat <<JEOF
{"jobs": [{"name": "PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard 2/3)", "conclusion": "$1", "steps": $steps}]}
JEOF
}

echo "watchdog_trip_selftest (gh-2290):"

# AC1 — the gh-2290 kill mode (the REAL shape: conclusion cancelled,
# mid-flight step cancelled, trailing always()-evidence steps skipped).
out="$(fixture ac1 "$(json_for cancelled kill)")"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=true" ]
check "AC1 cancelled job with a cancelled step trips (gh-2290 kill mode)" $?

out="$(fixture ac2 "$(json_for failure kill)")"

check "FC1a real test failure (failed step, trailing evidence) does NOT trip" $?

out="$(fixture fc1b '{"jobs": [{"name": "Core tests (shard 3/4)", "conclusion": "failure", "steps": [{"name": "setup", "conclusion": "success"}, {"name": "dart test", "conclusion": "failure"}]}]}')"

check "FC1b real test failure (failed LAST step) does NOT trip" $?

# FC2 — clean, skipped, never-started, empty.
out="$(fixture fc2a '{"jobs": [{"name": "Static gates", "conclusion": "success", "steps": [{"name": "analyze", "conclusion": "success"}]}]}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC2a success job does not trip" $?

out="$(fixture fc2b '{"jobs": [{"name": "Golden suite (macOS baselines)", "conclusion": "skipped", "steps": []}]}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC2b skipped job does not trip" $?

out="$(fixture fc2c '{"jobs": [{"name": "Binaries smoke gate", "conclusion": "cancelled", "steps": []}]}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC2c cancelled never-started job (no steps) does not trip" $?

out="$(fixture fc2d '{"jobs": []}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC2d empty jobs array does not trip" $?

check "RG4 multiple matches trip once, one line" $?

[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=true" ]
check "RG5 stdin arm trips" $?

The reviewer says this is tautological — `grep -vE '^trip='` strips every trip=-prefixed line, so the second `grep -qE '^trip='` can never match and the check can never fail. #   --scope all   Run every stage.

#   --scope app   analyze + dup + dupx + flutter.
#   --scope docs  analyze only.

**Fixed** in commit `4a8d949c96` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, the watchdog "Detect a timeout-type failure" step).

## What changed

- Deleted the duplicated back-to-back invocation. The trip step now runs the check exactly once:

  ```yaml
  run: |
    gh run view "$RUN_ID" --repo "$REPO" --json jobs > watchdog-jobs.json
    bash scripts/watchdog_trip_check.sh watchdog-jobs.json
  ```

- Agreed the second call carried no retry semantics: the script is pure (same input file, no network, no state), so a re-run cannot change the verdict. One invocation now owns `GITHUB_OUTPUT` — exactly one `trip=<bool>` line, and no doubled `::notice::`/job-listing diagnostics in the watchdog log.

## While there (review's ranked next-step)

- Dropped the dead jq call in `scripts/watchdog_trip_check.sh` (`printf … | jq -r "$projection | .[]" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true`). Verified it was pure dead weight: `$projection` ends in `| length`, so appending `| .[]` always errors (`Cannot iterate over number`), with stdout/stderr discarded and the exit swallowed by `|| true`. Old-vs-new script output is **byte-identical** on 5 fixtures (kill mode, real failure, never-started cancel, malformed JSON, empty array — the negative cases included).

## Regression guard (TDD)

- New test in `test/ci_watchdog_tag_retrigger_guard_test.dart` (AC3 group): *the trip step invokes `watchdog_trip_check.sh` EXACTLY once (one `trip=` line in GITHUB_OUTPUT)* — written first and failing against the old yaml (`Expected: <1>`, `Actual: <2>`), green after the fix.
- `dart test test/ci_watchdog_tag_retrigger_guard_test.dart` — **16 passed**.
- `bash scripts/watchdog_trip_selftest.sh` — **all green** (15/15, incl. RG3 "exactly one `trip=` line lands in `GITHUB_OUTPUT`").
- `dart analyze` / `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` on the touched test file — clean.

Not picked up this lap (left for triage): the ranked-digest note that selftest RG2's `grep -vE '^trip=' | grep -qE '^trip='` chain is vacuous — real, but it needs new assertion semantics rather than a line removal, and it was not part of the review's next steps.

# PR #2296 rework — gh-2290 [ci-red] v1.0.745 failed

Rework lap for PR #2296 (`ai/gh-2290` → `main`). One open review thread, no owned CI failures, no merge conflicts.

## Issues/Notes

- **Owned CI violations: none.** `ci_failures.md` reports "No Failed Checks" on the rework head — there is no "Violations you must fix (N owned)" table, and `ci_failures_full.log` does not exist. Nothing to fix or dispute on the CI leg.
- **Digest item left for triage:** the ranked-digest note that `scripts/watchdog_trip_selftest.sh` RG2 (`grep -vE '^trip=' | grep -qE '^trip='`) is a vacuous assertion is real, but it was not part of the review's Next Steps and needs new assertion semantics (not a line removal) — not picked up this lap.
- **Digest note (operational, no code change possible here):** merging does not make the `v1.0.745` tag itself green — that ref carries the old watchdog-less `ci.yml`. Per ticket gh-2290 ("Closes manually when the ref goes green"), the follow-up is a manual `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref v1.0.745` (or let the next tag supersede). Deliberately not dispatched from this rework lap — workflow dispatch is ticket-lifecycle action, not PR code.
- **Environment note:** a repo-wide `dart format --set-exit-if-changed --output=none .` under local SDK 3.14.0 flags 412 pre-existing files across the tree (200 test, 118 flutter_app, 30 lib, …) — a formatter version-skew vs. the repo's formatting profile, present before this lap and outside this PR's files. Untouched per the surgical scope guard; only the file this lap touched was formatted.

## Approach

TDD (RED → GREEN → REFACTOR) on the single open thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc644EjI` (⚠️ IMPORTANT, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`):

1. **RED** — extended `test/ci_watchdog_tag_retrigger_guard_test.dart` (AC3 group) with a test pinning that the watchdog trip step invokes `scripts/watchdog_trip_check.sh` **exactly once** (each invocation appends a `trip=<bool>` line to `GITHUB_OUTPUT` — the RG3 contract the PR itself pins). Ran it against the unfixed tree: failed as expected (`Expected: <1>` / `Actual: <2>`).
2. **GREEN** — deleted the duplicated `bash scripts/watchdog_trip_check.sh watchdog-jobs.json` line from the trip step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Test turned green.
3. **While there** (the review's ranked next-step, same invocation chain): removed the dead jq call in `scripts/watchdog_trip_check.sh` — `$projection` ends in `| length`, so `"$projection | .[]"` always errors (`Cannot iterate over number`) with output discarded to `/dev/null` and the exit swallowed by `|| true`. Verified old-vs-new script output is **byte-identical** on 5 fixtures (kill mode, real failure, never-started cancel, malformed JSON, empty array — negative cases included).
4. **REFACTOR** — `dart format` on the touched test file only (also normalizes the digest-flagged non-format-clean `_jobSteps` helper), re-ran the full targeted verification.

Commit: `4a8d949c96` `ci(gh-2290): watchdog trip step invokes the trip check once` (pushed; content identical to the harness WIP auto-save `f7a520614c`, whose tree the commit documents — force-push of the amend was blocked by the push safety guard, so the clean message rides a follow-up commit on the identical tree).

## Files Modified

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — trip step: removed the duplicated `watchdog_trip_check.sh` invocation (1 line).
- `scripts/watchdog_trip_check.sh` — removed the dead jq projection call (2 lines); no behavior change (proven fixture-identical).
- `test/ci_watchdog_tag_retrigger_guard_test.dart` — new AC3 regression test (single invocation) + `dart format` normalization of the helper.

## Test Coverage

- `dart test test/ci_watchdog_tag_retrigger_guard_test.dart` — **16 passed** (15 pre-existing + 1 new; the new test failed before the fix and passes after).
- `bash scripts/watchdog_trip_selftest.sh` — **all green** (15/15 fixtures, incl. RG3 one-`trip=`-line-in-`GITHUB_OUTPUT` and the negative cases: real failure, never-started cancel, malformed JSON, empty array).
- Old-vs-new `watchdog_trip_check.sh` parity — byte-identical stdout/exit on all 5 crafted fixtures.
- `dart analyze test/ci_watchdog_tag_retrigger_guard_test.dart` — No issues found.
- `dart format --set-exit-if-changed --output=none` on the touched test file — clean.
- `ci.yml` YAML-parse sanity — parses OK; 55 jobs, watchdog steps = 5 (unchanged from the PR's stated baseline), trip-step check-script invocations = 1.

No product Dart code (`lib/`, `bin/`, packages) is touched by this lap, so the product test surface is unchanged; CI re-runs the full gate on the PR head.
